info.desc: Blue Lines is the debut studio album by English electronic music group Massive Attack, released on April 8, 1991 by Wild Bunch and Virgin Records. Generally regarded as the first "trip hop" album, Blue Lines blended elements of hip hop (such as breakbeats, sampling and rapping) with dub, soul, reggae and electronic music. The recording was led by members Grantley "Daddy G" Marshall, Robert "3D" Del Naja, Adrian "Tricky" Thaws and Andrew "Mushroom" Vowles, with co-production by Jonny Dollar. It also features contributions by singers Shara Nelson and Horace Andy. Blue Lines was named the 21st greatest album of all .

podcast.body: During the recording sessions for *Blue Lines*, the three founding members of Massive Attack were present in the studio, along with Tricky, described as a "strange member" of the group. Also in attendance was a young production assistant named Geoff Barrow, who would later found Portishead. This convergence of key figures in a single studio is considered a pivotal moment for the gestation of the Trip Hop movement. "Durante la grabación del Blue Line se habían juntado los tres miembros a Masyl Atac con Tricky, que era ese extraño miembro de Masyl Atac, pero también había un joven físimo ayudante de producción, que era músico que estaba empezando, que se llamaba Jeop Barrow."

podcast.body: Released as the first album by Massive Attack, it is almost consensually considered the first Trip Hop record, although some might disagree on its groundbreaking nature. It was heavily influenced by soul music, black music, downtempo, reggae, and American hip hop movements. "crean lo que es el primer disco de Trip Hop que es el Blue Lines."

Released in 1991, this album is credited with marking the beginning of an entirely new musical style: trip hop. It stands out because, unlike grunge, rock, or rap, it provides a definitive starting point for its genre. Widely considered one of the most important albums in music history, it is praised for its complexity and completeness, blending electronic music with pop, reggae, jazz, hip hop, soul, and funk. "nunca nada había sido como ese disco."

podcast.body: This debut album, released in 1991, marked a significant turning point in European electronic music. Critics hailed it as the "Kind of Blue of rave culture" because Massive Attack skillfully stripped Hip Hop's raw rhythms of their urban urgency, reduced BPMs, and infused them with a sensual, soulful atmosphere complemented by dub-influenced basslines, effectively inventing the introspective music style of the decade. "El disco supuso nantes y en después en la música electrónica europea, la crítica lo definió como el kind of blue de la cultura de ens."
